Power off. Unplug. Control static. Then look inside.

::: {.tej-safety-strip}
`POWER OFF`{=html}

`UNPLUG`{=html}

`HOLD POWER 10 s`{=html}

`CONTROL STATIC`{=html}

`HANDLE EDGES`{=html}

`NEVER OPEN THE PSU`{=html}
:::

::: {.callout-important title="Before the case opens"}
Shut down, unplug wall power and peripherals, then hold the power button for about 10 seconds. Work on a clean, dry, non-carpeted surface. Use the approved antistatic procedure. Never open the metal power-supply enclosure.
:::

:::

## What is inside?

:::: {.tej-visual-grid}
::: {.tej-visual-card}
### Motherboard

The main circuit board. It connects the CPU, RAM, storage, power, ports, and expansion cards.
:::

::: {.tej-visual-card}
### CPU

Runs program instructions. A heat sink and fan usually cover it.
:::

::: {.tej-visual-card}
### RAM

Fast working memory for programs in use now. It clears when power is removed.
:::

::: {.tej-visual-card}
### Power supply

Converts wall AC to the low-voltage DC used by the computer. Inspect only the outside, cables, and label.
:::

::: {.tej-visual-card}
### Cooling

Fans, heat sinks, vents, and thermal material move heat away from chips.
:::

::: {.tej-visual-card}
### Expansion parts

Graphics, Wi-Fi, network, and sound cards add functions. Not every computer has every part.
:::
::::

## SSD or spinning hard disk?

:::: {.tej-visual-grid}
::: {.tej-visual-card}
![A hard disk drive beside a solid-state drive.](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/Special:Redirect/file/Maxtor_HDD_and_Intel_SSD_20100117.jpg)

### HDD: spinning disk

Magnetic platters spin under a moving read/write head. Usually cheaper per terabyte, but slower, noisier, and easier to damage while spinning.

*Figure 2. HDD and SSD. [Open source and licence.](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Maxtor_HDD_and_Intel_SSD_20100117.jpg)*
:::

::: {.tej-visual-card}
![M.2 solid-state drive circuit board.](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/Special:Redirect/file/SSD_M.2.svg)

### SSD: flash storage

Stores data in electronic flash memory. No moving parts. Usually faster, silent, lower-power, and more resistant to bumps.

*Figure 3. M.2 SSD. [Open source and licence.](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:SSD_M.2.svg)*
:::
::::

## How storage connects

:::: {.tej-visual-grid}
::: {.tej-visual-card}
![The data and power connectors on a SATA solid-state drive.](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/Special:Redirect/file/2015_Z%C5%82%C4%85cza_SATA_w_dysku_SSD.jpg)

### SATA drive: two connections

**SATA data** is the narrow 7-pin path to the motherboard. **SATA power** is the wider 15-pin path to the power supply.

*Figure 4. SATA connectors. [Open source and licence.](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:2015_Z%C5%82%C4%85cza_SATA_w_dysku_SSD.jpg)*
:::

::: {.tej-visual-card}
![M.2 storage board ready to mount in a motherboard slot.](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/Special:Redirect/file/SSD_M.2.svg)

### M.2 drive: mounts on the board

M.2 describes the shape. The drive may use SATA or NVMe/PCIe. The drive and motherboard slot must support the same type.
:::
::::

## Try it

With the computer unplugged, point to each visible part. Say its name and job before touching it. Use the teacher's motherboard photograph for the model-specific close-up.
